title: Stage dispatch and settlement
summary: A run settles its own target after required delivery and gates pass. A member still owing another named target's post-deploy QA or manual acceptance stays open, with no fabricated pass or waiver. Refusals name the item, requirement, phase, target and recovery. Lost responses remain unknown: read the exact preparation receipt or existing provider attempt before retrying or failing; pending attempts are preserved. An HTTPS response timeout on scoped-QA dispatch first waits for the existing reservation and recorded result using its identical request envelope over HTTPS in up to ten 60-second waits, never the self-deploy database door. A recovery without an answer remains resumable. Other lost scoped-QA dispatch answers are re-sent, since dispatch is idempotent: up to three sends, 5s then 15s apart, never a refusal. Past the last send it leaves the run in its QA stage and executing, so live QA keeps writing and the next re-drive continues. A failed stage records run status before the stage; a refused status write reports run_failure_unrecorded and changes neither. A member's QA plan configuration refusal, such as qa_plan_source_snapshot_missing, holds only that member: the stage records a qa_configuration_refused blocker with the recovery, wakes that member's owner once per wait, and keeps waiting on the other members. The driver does not exit for it. The run stays executing at its QA stage and recorded QA is kept. Fleet preparation exposes current subphases, pending heartbeats, elapsed time and reader counts in the existing driver capture. Copy-scoped batches preserve every canonical reader check and physical connection closure. When a bounded scoped-QA wait ends with blockers, the driver retains the awaiting-QA outcome even if the subsequent diagnostic report read fails. It labels fresh details unavailable and preserves the last known blocker diagnostic without fresh counts, success or gate waiver. Member settlement credits exact member-bound item cases. Each open plan group is gated once as a run-scoped subject; dispatch launches nothing and wakes no member for it, and sends one run-scoped notice listing pending groups with their run commands to the live run driver, else the live starting session, else steering. Only a new set of pending groups re-sends it. A group failure sends one notice naming its report and items and releases no member. A member removed while dispatch prepares its QA refuses as deployment_member_removed under the run lock, and dispatch skips it. A dispatch whose database lock wait is cancelled or times out answers qa_stage_dispatch_interrupted with the SQLSTATE, or run_busy for a run row held past its 2-second bound, and the lock holder as a held QA wait: the run stays executing at the stage and the driver re-dispatches it. The gate holds the run lock only for each acceptance write and commits it, so a dispatch walk never carries the lock into the next member. Materialize, rematerialize and removal read run-wide groups before the run row lock, which covers a fingerprint re-check and the writes. A run that changed in between is read again with the lock released; after three changed reads the call refuses as run_busy (run_read_changed) and the caller retries. Scoped QA waits poll a cheap run fingerprint and dispatch only on changed facts or the wait deadline. Gate reads share one run cache; acceptance writes re-check their subject under the lock. That re-check reads only its own member's frozen snapshot, never the whole run's. An accepted member already past its release wait skips the run-wide acceptance read; each remaining member gets only its own close-out route read fresh before acting. A dispatch attempts every accepted member's close-out, refused or not, and starts no more work after five seconds; a skipped member closes on a later dispatch or at settlement without holding the stage. QA wait wakes are withdrawn by the event that settles them (run terminal, member removed, member stage credited, member item closed). A dispatch wakes a waiting member only when no uncancelled wake for that same wait (run, stage, member, target) is stored, read once per call, so re-polling an unchanged wait sends nothing. Acknowledge and relay claim never re-read open waits, so their cost does not grow with the fleet. The driver retains its startup actor binding. Closed connections and failed database actor lookups yield resumable connection loss. Immutable release-file and published-record inputs are resolved once before dispatch writes, with no database transaction open during Git, GitHub or HTTP calls. Unexpected uncached source I/O refuses as deployment_qa_source_inputs_changed with a re-drive recovery. A failed rollback preserves the original error in the connection-loss answer, including idle-in-transaction timeouts. Execution settlement reloads current ownership under the existing membership/run/execution locks after result commits. Inherited QA can finish before its successor deploys, but stage acceptance and member close-out still wait for that owner's normal prerequisites and human gates. Deployment failure preserves inherited work; explicit cancellation and real removal retain cleanup.
